chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When one of you is invited to a meal, let him not let his child follow him, for if he does, he will be eating unlawfully and entering as a usurper.

key_terms.غَاصِباً: Usurper / One who takes by right or force
key_terms.يَسْتَتْبِعَنَّ: Let him make follow / Let him bring along

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bringing children to an invitation if they eat the food?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that bringing an uninvited child to a meal risks the child consuming food without the host's explicit consent, thereby rendering the consumption 'haram' and the child a 'ghasib' (usurper). This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise social etiquette (adab) and the legal concept of entitlement, distinguishing between general hospitality and specific invitation to avoid inadvertent violation of the host's property rights.
